items.title: Somalia: NISA Arrests 11 Al-Shabaab Operatives in Security Operations Around Mogadishu
items.description: NISA said its forces arrested 11 operatives linked to the networks, which were allegedly being prepared to carry out activities threatening security. The networks were dismantled during planned security operations conducted in Darussalam, Garasbaley, Kahda, Daynile, and Afgoye. NISA forces also seized weapons and other materials that the operatives allegedly intended to use in their planned activities. The operations are part of NISA's ongoing efforts to prevent Al-Shabaab and other terrorist groups from carrying out activities aimed at undermining security and harming the Somali people.
items.titleIt: Somalia: NISA Arrests 11 Al-Shabaab Operatives in Security Operations Around Mogadishu

items.title: The Signature That Never Comes: Why Somalia's Clan Killers Walk Free
items.description: A death sentence in Somalia isn't final until the president signs it. Increasingly, none of them do.   That piece traced how Ahmed Shire Hussein, a Somali National Army soldier, was executed on camera near El Baraf for the crime of his father's clan — one entry in a pattern of hit squads, informant networks, and a tribal shield strong enough that a court willing to execute Al-Shabaab fighters would not touch a killer protected by his own sub-clan. items.titleIt: The Signature That Never Comes: Why Somalia's Clan Killers Walk Free

items.description: Speaking after his son's funeral at Muuse Boqor Mosque the following day, veteran journalist Maxamed Cumar Baakaay put words to what the killing meant: "Allah gave me my son, and now Allah has taken him back. I praise Him. We have survived so many historic atrocities here in Mogadishu, only for me to lose my boy to the blades of the Ciyaal Weero." items.title: The Anatomy of a Blood Debt: How Clan Revenge Killings are Fracturing Somalia's Frontlines
items.description: Before he was executed, a chilling video captured his final moments. Stranded and defenseless, Hussein looked directly at his armed captors and uttered a devastating plea: "Abtiyaalow, ha i dilina" ("Maternal uncles, do not kill me"). The phrase was not just a desperate cry for mercy — according to clan elders and opposition figures interviewed for this piece, it reflected a specific and devastating reality. items.title: Switzerland plans deportation of seriously injured Somali citizen
items.description: As we have learnt from two individuals affected, Swiss police authorities use an enormous amount of violence during forced deportations. From the perspective of lawyers and Swiss human rights organisations, the authorities are thereby committing massive violations of Swiss and international law. Furthermore, in at least two cases, they have put the lives of those affected at serious risk. Augenauf shares this assessment and has informed the relevant authorities (including the commander of the Zurich cantonal police and the National Commission for the Prevention of Torture, NKVF). Bot
items.titleIt: Switzerland plans deportation of seriously injured Somali citizen

items.titleIt: Somali journalist Bashir Mohamed Abdullahi dies after being shot during Baidoa clashes
